newsitem.title: USA: NFL-PACKERS' BEEBE DETERMINED TO AVOID FIFTH SUPER BOWL LOSS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-PACKERS' BEEBE DETERMINED TO AVOID FIFTH SUPER BOWL LOSS.

text.p: Green Bay Packers receiver Don Beebe has accumulated vast Super Bowl experience in his eight years in the National Football League, almost all of it miserable.
Beebe is preparing for his fifth Super Bowl this week, more than any player on either the Packers or New England Patriots, who will square off in Super Bowl XXXI on Sunday.
Unfortunately his first four was as a member of the Buffalo Bills, who lost four consecutive Super Bowls from 1991-1994.
The 32-year-old father of three said Wednesday he had been the butt of a standing joke in Green Bay the past two weeks with teammates telling him 'you got us here, now you can go.'

"I said 'no way, you're crazy, I'm not going anywhere, I'm going to win this sucker,'" said Beebe, who keeps his four AFC championship rings in a mahogany box with a space in the middle awaiting the one that got away -- four times.

"In the early '90s the Buffalo Bills were the winningest franchise ... and we're going to be labeled as losers, which is a shame because we were winners," said Beebe, who sat out the first Buffalo loss with a broken leg, but played the next three.
"I don't think the team handled adversity in the Super Bowl very well," he said of the Bills' penchant for costly turnovers in the big game.
"Emotions got so low so fast. It seemed like when we made mistakes they multiplied into more mistakes. We'd turn the ball over and it resulted in another turnover and another turnover."
Beebe says these Green Bay Packers never seem to get rattled by adversity, even in big games.

"There's great leadership on this team, that makes you a little more confient," he said. "If I win this, it will be in sports the greatest thing I've ever experienced. I just get goosebumps thinking about it.
"The disappointment will be erased, no doubt about it."

Beebe said many of his former Buffalo teammates will be pulling for him Sunday, although he hasn't spoken with Gale Gilbert, the backup quarterback who left the Bills for the San Diego Chargers just in time to lose a record fifth consecutive Super Bowl.
After the San Diego loss to the 49ers two years ago, Beebe said of his fellow Bills: "We all called Gale and said 'maybe it was you.'"
He's not calling Gilbert this week.
"I don't even want to talk to Gale. I don't want to know what Gale has to say," Beebe said, shaking his head.
"He stands alone (as a five-time loser) and hopefully he will stand alone for another year."
Beebe, who stepped up and had some big games for Green Bay when the team's receiver corps was decimated by injuries this season, is concentrating on being more calm this time around.
"My first Super Bowl my emotions were so high I didn't know what to do," he recalled.
"I know what's at stake here and I know what can happen. And if I lost this one, then this whole season was for nothing," he said.
"I want this to be the best game I've ever played."
Asked what he might do to celebrate if he finally earns that precious Super Bowl ring, Beebe said: "I'm trying not to think about it because I'll start crying now.
